name: Eliashib
overview: The name Eliashib appears multiple times in Scripture, primarily associated with priestly roles and leadership among the Israelites. Notably, Eliashib is identified as a high priest who actively participated in rebuilding and sanctifying Jerusalem's gates, demonstrating his commitment to God's house (Nehemiah 3:1). Additionally, Eliashib is mentioned as a priest overseeing the temple chambers, though he faced challenges due to alliances that compromised his duties (Nehemiah 13:4). The genealogical records also highlight Eliashib's place in the priestly lineage, being the son of Joiakim and father of Joiada (Nehemiah 12:10). Beyond the high priest, the name refers to several Israelites listed in Ezra, including descendants of Elioenai and members involved in temple service, underscoring the name's significance in the post-exilic community (Ezra 10:24, 27, 36).
